sections.skill: Choose a small, cheap test that answers one question

questions.prompt: Which is the best small test for a homemade granola idea?

choices.text: Design packaging for 20 flavors right away
Wait a year to perfect the recipe in private
Sell 30 bags at a weekend farmers market
Rent a factory to make 50,000 bags first

questions.correct_answer: Sell 30 bags at a weekend farmers market
questions.intro: Before spending a lot, test a small version of the idea. A small test is cheap, quick, and answers one question, such as "Will people book a pet-sitting visit?" Examples: offering a service to a few customers, selling 20 handmade items at one market, a simple sign-up page, or a pre-order. A good test has a clear question, a small cost, a time limit, and a result you decide in advance would count as success. Testing first avoids building something large that nobody buys.
questions.feedback: A small market test is cheap and shows whether people buy.

questions.prompt: Why is a lemonade stand a good test before a juice company?

choices.text: It is the only way to sell drinks.
It guarantees the juice company will succeed.
It costs little and shows whether people pay.

questions.correct_answer: It costs little and shows whether people pay.
questions.intro: Think of opening a lemonade stand before building a juice company. The stand costs little, runs one afternoon, and answers a real question: will people stop and pay? If yes, you learn prices and favorite flavors. If no, you lost a few dollars, not your savings. A small test is the smallest step that teaches you something true about customers. Big plans can come after small tests show promise.
questions.feedback: A cheap step that reveals real buying behavior.
